money_at_stake.basis: No dated source sizes the incremental spend, capex, or revenue pool this specific STAREE readout moves. Two independently sourced market reports were fetched and re-verified this run and price the EXISTING global statin and atorvastatin markets: USD 17.1bn in 2026 [Persistence Market Research, Statins Market, as of 2026-05-01, https://www.persistencemarketresearch.com/market-research/statins-market.asp -- confirmed verbatim on the page: "The global statins market size is expected to reach US$ 17.1 billion in 2026"] and USD 14.48bn in 2026 [The Business Research Company, Atorvastatin Global Market Report, as of 2026-07-01, https://www.thebusinessresearchcompany.com/report/atorvastatin-global-market-report -- confirmed verbatim: "It will grow from $13.11 billion in 2025 to $14.48 billion in 2026 at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.5%."]. Both size the market as it already stands under current prescribing practice, which exists regardless of this trial; neither is a citation of what THIS occurrence moves, because no guideline body has yet acted on STAREE and there is no dated estimate of how many additional over-70 patients would be newly prescribed, what added lipid/liver-function monitoring spend follows them, or what offsetting reduction in cardiac-procedure volume a 30% relative-risk cut produces system-wide. The nearest historical analogy, general reporting that the 2013 ACC/AHA cholesterol guideline expansion added roughly 12.8 million statin-eligible US adults and lifted national statin prescription volume on the order of 25 to 65%, shows a guideline-driven statin expansion CAN move real volume, but translating that prior episode's scale onto this one (a narrower 70-plus-only, already-partially-treated slice, in a trial with no announced guideline-revision date) would be exactly the reasoned-but-unsourced estimate method section 0.2 forbids on this leg. Searched and not found: STAREE-specific analyst or market commentary dated to the 2026-08-29/08-30 readout window; any dollar translation of the over-70 statin-eligible-but-untreated population. Leg is NULL rather than anchored to the pre-existing base-market figure, because using that figure would overstate what this specific occurrence, on its own, moves. Because this leg carries no evidence array (nothing here clears the cited-or-NULL bar), it is exempt from the source_excerpt requirement, which applies only to evidence items on a scored leg; the two figures quoted above were nonetheless fetched and verified this run rather than left as unopened URLs.

public_reach.rationale: Unlike the Arctic occurrence this stage was built to test against, nothing in this chain is sanctioned or state-monopolized: the manufacturing base is a fragmented set of competing, mostly listed pharmaceutical companies. Two independently sourced 2026 market reports each name a long roster of manufacturers of this exact molecule and drug class: the atorvastatin report's own company sentence names 23, and the statins report's company-coverage list names 20. The large majority of the names that recur across both lists (Zydus Lifesciences, Pfizer, Viatris, Teva, Sun Pharmaceutical, Dr. Reddy's, Merck, AstraZeneca, Novartis, Lupin, Aurobindo) are listed issuers; a minority (Centrient Pharmaceuticals, AdvaCare Pharma) are privately held. That argues for real listed reach. Against it: none of these companies is a pure play on atorvastatin or on this guideline shift, a decades-old off-patent generic is a rounding error inside each of their much larger diversified portfolios, and the largest additional spend this occurrence could plausibly drive, primary-care prescribing plus lipid and liver-function monitoring, is administered through public and nonprofit health systems (the trial itself was recruited through Australian general practice) rather than through investable equity. Scored at the middle anchor, 'clearly reachable, mixed,' rather than higher: reach exists without concentrating anywhere a chain build could point to as a pure play.

capture_odds.rationale: Atorvastatin is close to the textbook case of a fully genericized commodity molecule. The same two market reports that establish reach also establish the absence of pricing power: 23 named competing manufacturers in the atorvastatin report and 20 in the statins report sell one off-patent drug, so no single maker can raise price without an immediate substitution to any of a dozen-plus qualified generic alternatives, the anchor definition of a commodity, price-taker market rather than a concentrated, qualification-locked one. The one part of this chain with genuine capture power, cardiac interventional device and procedure makers whose volume a 30% relative-risk reduction would erode over time, sits on the wrong side of this specific trade: this occurrence is a headwind to their existing captured profit, not a source of new capture for them. No evidence was found of any player positioned to capture incremental profit from this specific finding.

timing_fit.rationale: The underlying evidence is already in hand and dated at the very start of the window: STAREE is a completed trial, presented at the European Society of Cardiology Congress (Aug. 28-31, 2026, Munich) and reported the same day, with lead investigator Francois Mach quoted framing the result as removing age as a reason to withhold statins. That places the scientific trigger for any prescribing or guideline change inside the occurrence's own anchor date. Not scored higher, because nothing found commits any guideline body to a revision date: multi-society guideline panels historically take one to several years to formally revise primary-prevention thresholds after a single pivotal trial, and routine-prescribing adoption then lags the guideline itself. No dated announcement of a scheduled guideline review was found. Scored 'credible inside the window' rather than 'committed and dated', because a completed trial with no confirmed guideline-revision date is a weaker timing claim than the signed, under-construction contracts this stage's own exemplar appraisal was able to cite. The Guardian citation this leg previously carried alongside Healio was dropped this run: WebFetch cannot reach www.theguardian.com in this environment and no Wayback Machine snapshot of that URL exists (checked via the Wayback availability API, zero snapshots returned), so it is unverifiable per method section 1 and was removed rather than repaired. Every material fact it supported (participant count, mean age, sex split, dose, follow-up, event counts, hazard ratio, and the investigator quote) is independently and verbatim confirmed via Healio, fetched and quoted this run, so the leg's scoring is unaffected.

evidence.claim: STAREE, presented at the European Society of Cardiology Congress (Aug. 28-31, 2026, Munich), randomised 9,971 older adults with no history of CVD, diabetes or dementia, mean age 75 (51.9% women), to atorvastatin 40 mg once daily (n=4,984) or placebo (n=4,987); over an average 6-year follow-up, primary CV events occurred in 297 of the statin group versus 412 of the placebo group, HR 0.7 (95% CI 0.61-0.82).
evidence.source_name: Healio, Statins cut risk for first heart attack, stroke by 30% after age 70
source_excerpt: Presented at: European Society of Cardiology Congress; Aug. 28-31, 2026; Munich.

The STAREE trial included 9,971 older adults with no history of CVD, diabetes or dementia at baseline with a mean age of 75 years (51.9% women), randomly assigned to receive atorvastatin 40 mg once daily (n = 4,984) or placebo (n = 4,987).

Primary CV events occurred among 297 participants in the statin group and 412 participants in the placebo group, for an HR of 0.7 (95% CI, 0.61-0.82; P < .001) and a number needed to treat of 37 to prevent a major CV event over the average follow-up of 6 years.

notes.text: Nell's dated claim was verified independently this run against Medscape, Healio, TCTMD and the American College of Cardiology's own ESC-2026 session page, all of which corroborate the exact trial statistics on the candidate card (9,971 participants, mean age 74.7, 52% female, atorvastatin 40mg, 6-year follow-up, 30% relative reduction, 6.0% vs 8.3% event rates, no disability-free-survival benefit). The claim holds. The candidate's own note flagged this as a test of whether the LEAKY/THIN bands do real work; the actual result is UNRANKED, one level earlier than either: nobody has published a number for what this specific guideline-relevant finding is worth, so there is nothing yet to call thin or leaky. public_reach (50) and capture_odds (15) are scored and evidenced regardless, so a future re-run that finds a money figure only needs to fill the one leg, not redo the appraisal.
